subject: Re: Benchmark A/B test — Redwood vs hyperscaler (latency & throughput)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Benchmark A/B test — Redwood vs hyperscaler (post-call recap and next steps)

Hi Alex —

Nice to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

What we heard from you:
- Primary goal: reduce inference latency for interactive features (p95/p99 targets) while keeping token cost in check.
- Typical request profile: seq len ~512, concurrency bursts up to 40, steady-state bursty traffic ~20 threads.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 < 200ms and p99 < 500ms for 1-2k tokens per request, or clear TCO win vs current provider.

What Redwood delivered during the A/B run (summary):
- Redwood (A): p95 = 118ms, p99 = 385ms, throughput ~1,350 tokens/sec (single-node avg under your concurrency profile).
- Hyperscaler (B): p95 = 215ms, p99 = 720ms, throughput ~980 tokens/sec under same config.
- Notes: both runs used the same model family (open-variant you specified), identical batch window (20ms), and identical client-side concurrency. Redwood run used our quantization-profile-2 + KV cache warm.

Attachments: I attached the raw CSV with per-run samples and the short latency report (redwood_vs_hyperscaler_abtest_results.csv, latency_p95_p99_report.pdf). Also included run-configs.txt with exact flags and kernel notes.

Suggested next steps:
1) Quick technical sync (30m) with your infra/ML infra team to review traces + tail logs — propose Tue 5/18 10:00am PT.
2) If you want, we can run a dedicated-capacity trial for 2 weeks to validate at your production traffic pattern.
3) Share any additional acceptance criteria (cost targets, cold-start windows) and we’ll run a targeted AB with those constraints.

Let me know which time works for the sync and if there are any other folks we should include.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0138

Subject: Re: Benchmark A/B test — Redwood vs hyperscaler (answers + expanded metrics)

Hi Alex — quick answers inline and a couple extra charts attached.

- Cold-starts: the numbers in the summary are steady-state (warm) after KV cache warmed. We ran a separate cold-start sweep — median cold-start for Redwood was ~420ms, hyperscaler median cold-start ~1.1s. See latency_p95_p99_report.pdf (page 2).
- Token length: the CSV uses an average payload length of 612 tokens (we also ran a 256/1024 sweep; those are in the CSV).
- GPU utilization / memory: during the A run our nodes averaged 72% GPU utilization with model in 8-bit quantized footprint (~22GB VRAM effective). Hyperscaler nodes showed 88% utilization on the same load but had higher kernel overheads which contributed to tail latency. Full perf counters are in the CSV.

Additional datapoints you might care about:
- p95 by concurrency: 8c -> 92ms, 20c -> 118ms, 40c -> 165ms (Redwood).
- tokens/sec measured at 40 concurrent clients: Redwood ~1,100 tokens/sec steady, hyperscaler ~810 tokens/sec. (The summary above was for a 20c test.)

Next steps we propose for the sync:
- Walk the traces and tail stacks (2-3 traces).
- Confirm Dedicated trial sizing and duration.
- If Globex agrees, we’ll prepare a one-week on-prem-style load run with your traffic generator.

Looping Rafael and Dylan for any additional notes and to prep the trial ops playbook.

Thanks —
Marissa
